sections.normalized_html: What is the perimeter, in feet, of a rectangle with a length of [MATH: 15] feet and a width of [MATH: 6] feet?

sections.normalized_html:
To find the perimeter of a rectangle, we use the formula

[MATH: P = 2\ell + 2w,] where [MATH: \ell] is the length and [MATH: w] is the width.

We substitute the given values:

[MATH: P|= 2(15) + 2(6); = 30 + 12; = 42]

So, the perimeter is [MATH: 42] feet.

items.title: Finding a Side Length Given the Perimeter and Two Other Sides of a Triangle

sections.normalized_html: The perimeter of triangle [MATH: JKL] is [MATH: 36] meters. The length of side [MATH: JK] is [MATH: 11] meters, and the length of side [MATH: JL] is [MATH: 10] meters. What is the length, in meters, of side [MATH: KL?]
sections.readable_text: The perimeter of triangle [MATH: JKL] is [MATH: 36] meters. The length of side [MATH: JK] is [MATH: 11] meters, and the length of side [MATH: JL] is [MATH: 10] meters. What is the length, in meters, of side [MATH: KL?]

sections.normalized_html:
To find the missing side of a triangle, we use the perimeter formula, which is the sum of the lengths of its sides. In this case [MATH: P = JK + JL + KL.]

We substitute the known values into the formula and solve for [MATH: KL{:}] [MATH: 36|= 11 + 10 + KL; 36|= 21 + KL; 36 − 21|= KL; 15|= KL; KL|= 15]

So, the length of side [MATH: KL] is [MATH: 15\,\text{m}.]

sections.normalized_html: The side length of square [MATH: P] is [MATH: 8] meters. The perimeter of square [MATH: Q] is [MATH: 5] times the perimeter of square [MATH: P.] What is the side length, in meters, of square [MATH: Q?]
sections.readable_text: The side length of square [MATH: P] is [MATH: 8] meters. The perimeter of square [MATH: Q] is [MATH: 5] times the perimeter of square [MATH: P.] What is the side length, in meters, of square [MATH: Q?]

sections.normalized_html:
We are told that square [MATH: P] has a side length of [MATH: 8\,\text{m}.]

To find the perimeter of square [MATH: P,] we use the formula for the perimeter of a square [MATH: P = 4s.] Substituting [MATH: s = 8,] we get [MATH: P|= 4 ⋅ 8; = 32m.]

Let [MATH: P_Q] be the perimeter of square [MATH: Q.] We use the fact that it is [MATH: 5] times the perimeter of square [MATH: P{:}] [MATH: P_{Q}|= 5 ⋅ 32; = 160m]

To find the side length of square [MATH: Q,] we divide its perimeter by [MATH: 4{:}] [MATH: s = \frac{160}{4} = 40\, \text{m}]

So, the side length of square [MATH: Q] is [MATH: 40\,\text{m}.]
